title: Roos realization descends naturally through flat K-flat representatives
statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be finite and let $(\mathcal C_i,R_i)$ for $1\le i\le r$ and $(\mathcal C,R)$ be ringed sites small relative to their module universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $D(R_i)$ and $D(R)$ for their ordinary unbounded derived categories and $Q_i,Q$ for cochain localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P_i$ be the full category of K-flat complexes of $R_i$-modules with flat terms, with cochain maps [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and put $q=\prod_i Q_i|_{\mathcal P_i}$. Suppose countable products of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Let
$$Z:\prod_i\mathcal P_i\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$$
be a functor to complexes of strict inverse towers indexed by $n\ge1$ [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], carrying tuples of quasi-isomorphisms to levelwise quasi-isomorphisms. If $X$ is a strict tower complex, write
$$\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nX_n\to\prod_nX_n)[-1],\qquad s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1}),$$
and use the natural projection-compatible comparison $\rho_X:\mathsf C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X$ with its K-injective normalization [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, def-pur-kinjective-complex].

There exist functors $\overline Z:\prod_iD(R_i)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$ and $\widehat Z:\prod_iD(R_i)\to D(R)$ with natural representative identifications
$$\overline Zq\cong Q_{\rm Tow}Z,\qquad \widehat Zq\cong Q\mathsf C Z,$$
and a natural isomorphism $r_Z:\widehat Z\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\,\overline Z$. Its representative component is $\rho_{Z(P)}$: for a K-injective tower resolution $a:Z(P)\to I$ with injective terms it is $[\mathsf C(a)]$ followed by the inverse of $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with zero shifted coordinate. In particular it preserves the actual total-limit projections. It is natural for all morphisms of the derived inputs, including roofs of good representatives. The functors with their representative identifications, and $r_Z$ with the displayed representative components, are unique up to unique compatible natural isomorphism; replacing choices of good resolutions preserves these comparisons. No uniqueness from equality of level projections alone is asserted.

proof.text: The proved functorial_resolution helper in Sheaf.Algebra.Homology.RingedKFlatSingleTensorComparison supplies functorial flat-term K-flat resolutions with quasi-isomorphic counit. Lift this functor to the full category of TensorFlatRepresentative objects. The inclusion is fully faithful and the quasi-isomorphism class is its inverse image; LocalizerMorphism.isLocalizedEquivalence_of_functorial_left_resolutions and IsLocalizedEquivalence.isLocalization show that its composite with DerivedCategory.Q is a localization. This replaces the cylinder and homotopy-quotient argument.

Apply Mathlib Functor.IsLocalization.pi to the finite product of these localizations. HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation turns the assumed levelwise quasi-isomorphisms of Z into quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes. Localization.lift and Localization.fac construct Zbar and alpha.

Transport Grothendieck abelianness to the essentially small ringed site and to its tower category using the proved moduleSheaves_grothendieck and tower_grothendieck helpers in RingedStrictTowerHomotopyLimitIndependentCoefficients. The generic proved roos_map_quasiIso, roos_inclusion_quasiIso, and roos_universal helpers of StrictRoosDerivation give a localization lift CF of roosF and its right-derived universal property in the independent coefficient universe. rightDerivedUnique compares CF with the given RF. The unit equation follows from rightDerivedNatTrans_app. Define theta by composing the lift factorization and this comparison; put e(X,n)=theta(X) inverse followed by Q(roosEval X n).

Set Zhat=Zbar followed by RF and rZ to the identity isomorphism. Define beta from alpha whiskered by RF followed by theta inverse whiskered by Z. The component equation follows by cancellation. For any quasi-isomorphic K-injective resolution a:Z(P) to I, take eps=asIso(Q(roosι I)) and d=asIso(eta I) followed by the inverse of asIso(RF(Q(a))). Naturality of theta and its unit equation give the required normalization. Evaluation quasi-isomorphisms give ev; roosι_eval, roosEval_natural, and cancellation by ev prove the actual limit-projection equation.

Fully faithful restriction along q lifts alpha followed by alpha-prime inverse, and beta followed by beta-prime inverse, to unique natural isomorphisms u and v. The representative component equations and cancellation by RF(alpha-prime) show compatibility with rZ after q. Localization.natTrans_ext extends this equality to all derived inputs. The two individual uniqueness statements prove uniqueness of the pair, including its compatibility. Since these are natural transformations on the product derived category, the result covers roofs and changes of resolutions.

Terms are flat, and B is K-flat because the contraction survives the signed total tensor. A functor that inverts quasi-isomorphisms identifies homotopic maps without needing additivity. The step is long but written out completely, so I accept it as elementary. Step 2: the equivalence clause of the statement of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent (not its proof), together with Step 1 and the universal property, makes q_i a cochain localization; the site and commutative-ring hypotheses match. Step 3: lem-sfb-product-localization applies to the finite set {1..r} (identities are in W, no r≤4 limit); levelwise kernels and cokernels make cohomology levelwise, so Q_Tow Z inverts tuples and part (1) gives Z̄ and α. Step 6: parts (2) and (3) of lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property give uniqueness up to unique compatible isomorphism.
